transmission: Spores can spread from infected fallen leaves and susceptible host tissue; confirm locally.
symptoms: Olive to dark, roughly circular lesions may occur on leaves or fruit; visual symptoms are not diagnostic.
favorable_conditions: Prolonged leaf wetness and mild temperatures may favor infection; verify local disease guidance.
cultural_management: Remove or manage infected fallen leaves where locally recommended.
Use locally adapted resistant cultivars and maintain canopy airflow where appropriate.
biological_management: Use only locally registered biological products supported by qualified local guidance.
chemical_management: No curative claim is made. If chemical control is considered, confirm diagnosis and local registration, label, crop, and jurisdiction requirements.
differential_diagnosis: Other leaf or fruit spots, scab-like injury, and abiotic damage.
classes.jurisdiction: Unspecified; local extension guidance and product labels govern.

transmission: Phytophthora infestans can spread through airborne or water-dispersed sporangia and infected plant material; confirm local epidemiology.
symptoms: Rapidly expanding water-soaked lesions and sporulation may occur; seek prompt qualified confirmation because several problems can resemble it.
favorable_conditions: Cool to moderate temperatures with high humidity or prolonged leaf wetness may favor disease.
cultural_management: Seek local extension or plant-health advice promptly; manage infected material and volunteers only as locally directed.
biological_management: No biological treatment claim is made here; consult qualified local guidance and registration.
chemical_management: No cure is claimed. Any preventive or suppressive product must be locally registered and used strictly under its current crop-specific label and jurisdiction.
differential_diagnosis: Early blight, other foliar blights, frost injury, and other water-soaked lesions.
classes.jurisdiction: Unspecified; urgent local extension or plant-health guidance and product labels govern.
safety_notes: This image label is not a confirmed diagnosis; promptly verify suspected late blight with local experts.

transmission: Tomato mosaic virus can spread mechanically through contaminated hands, tools, or plant material; verify suspected cases.
symptoms: Mosaic or mottled leaves and growth changes may occur, but symptoms are not diagnostic.
favorable_conditions: Transmission risk can increase with plant handling and contaminated tools; environmental conditions alone do not confirm infection.
cultural_management: Use clean seed or transplants from reputable sources, sanitize tools using locally recommended methods, and remove confirmed infected plants as locally advised.
biological_management: No curative biological treatment is asserted.
chemical_management: There is no curative chemical treatment claim for this viral class. Chemicals must not be represented as curing the infected plant.
differential_diagnosis: Other viruses, herbicide injury, nutrient disorders, and physiological mosaic-like symptoms.
classes.jurisdiction: Unspecified; use local plant-health guidance and applicable labels for any permitted vector or sanitation product.
safety_notes: Viral diagnosis requires confirmation; do not promise chemical cure.

transmission: Tomato yellow leaf curl disease is associated with begomoviruses transmitted by whiteflies; verify locally.
symptoms: Leaf yellowing, curling, and stunting may occur; symptoms alone cannot confirm the virus.
favorable_conditions: Vector presence and conditions favoring whiteflies may influence risk; verify local epidemiology.
cultural_management: Use clean transplants and locally recommended exclusion, monitoring, and removal practices.
biological_management: Use only locally appropriate, registered biological vector-management options supported by qualified guidance; they do not cure infected plants.
chemical_management: No curative chemical treatment claim for the virus. Any vector control must be locally registered, label-compliant, and must not be described as curing infected plants.
differential_diagnosis: Other viruses, nutrient disorders, herbicide injury, and other causes of leaf curl.
classes.jurisdiction: Unspecified; local plant-health guidance and current product labels govern.
safety_notes: Viral class: no curative chemical claims. Vector management is not a cure.

transmission: Mites can move between plants by contact, wind, or infested material; this is a pest issue, not a pathogen infection.
symptoms: Fine stippling, bronzing, webbing, or mite presence may occur; inspect leaf undersides with magnification.
favorable_conditions: Hot, dry conditions can favor rapid mite increase; verify local conditions.
cultural_management: Confirm mites by inspection, monitor populations, reduce plant stress, and avoid practices that unnecessarily disrupt beneficial organisms.
biological_management: Conserve or use locally appropriate predatory mites and other beneficial organisms where supported by local IPM guidance.
chemical_management: If intervention is justified, choose only locally registered acaricide or other labeled category after confirming the pest; follow the label and protect beneficial organisms.
differential_diagnosis: Nutrient stress, other mite species, thrips injury, and abiotic stippling.
classes.jurisdiction: Unspecified; local IPM guidance and product labels govern.
safety_notes: Treat as an arthropod pest/IPM case, not a fungal, bacterial, or viral infection.
